home.heroText: I build durable interaction frameworks teams can ship, govern, and scale—especially where decisions carry consequences.
home.aboutBody:
Welcome to my site

I’ve spent much of my career working on things that have to hold up over time—under real constraints and in the hands of real people. What matters most to me is how systems behave once they’re in the wild, and whether people trust what they rely on every day.

Most of my work has taken place in complex environments rather than clean-slate projects. There is usually history, context, and trade-offs already driving decisions. That reality has shaped how I think about work: slowing down early, understanding what exists, and being deliberate about what gets introduced.

As experience has accumulated, my work ethic has changed. It’s become less about individual output and more about standards—how teams make decisions, and what behaviors we reinforce for our customers. I think often about designers coming up next, especially in an industry that moves quickly and doesn’t always leave room for judgment to develop.

Mentorship follows naturally from that responsibility. Sometimes it’s formal; often it’s not. Most of the time, it’s simply creating space to think clearly together. I care about leaving people stronger than I found them.

If any of this work lasts, it won’t be because of the artifacts alone. It will be because the thinking behind them continues through people who build deliberately and understand design as a form of stewardship.

articles.heroText:
These articles are published essays written outside the context of
          client work. They come from the same place as my design thinking, but move at a different pace.
articles.overviewBody:
I'm drawn to writing traditions that approach meaning
          differently—Persian philosophy, Irish poetry, and both Western and
          Eastern ways of shaping thought through language. Some writing leans
          into metaphor and patience, letting meaning unfold. Other traditions
          favor structure, clarity, and consequence. What holds my attention lives
          between those approaches—where feeling and discipline coexist, and where
          language is used to reveal rather than persuade. Each piece here stands
          on its own and is presented as originally published.

experience.heroSubtitle: Selected systems work, case studies, and outcomes.
experience.heroText:
These case studies reflect work on systems that operate across
          products, platforms, and organizations.
experience.overviewBody:
The focus is not on individual features, but on system-level
          structure—how multiple surfaces coexist, how behavior remains
          predictable at scale, and how decisions hold up over time. Each case
          examines a different layer of that problem, from foundational
          abstractions to global UI surfaces and embedded intelligence.

gallery.heroText:
A collection of visual work drawn from projects, explorations, and
          ongoing practice. Presented here without client context — the focus
          is on craft, composition, and care.
